summary: No new receipt to interpret this turn, so I consolidated the question's account and hardened the remaining liveness evidence. The parent interpretation now carries an explicit applicability summary for a reviewer: the trigger (RestoreCommittedLogs with a commit-tracking store, newest configuration entry at or below the persisted commit index, no covering snapshot), the three consequence classes with their retained control-backed receipts — missing membership context and no electability, decisions from the stale base (silent voter drop, two-server change, concurrent leaders, committed-entry truncation, FSM divergence), and stale-membership accounting (resurrected removed voter, forgotten added voter) — plus the boundary that any snapshot covering the newest configuration entry, or leaving the flag default, removes every observation, and that no in-protocol repair exists once the stale configuration is adopted. I also corrected a truncated receipt id in that summary rather than excusing it. Finally I requested one repeat of the three-voter simultaneous-restart experiment, since the headline progress claim (a live quorum of fully up-to-date voters unable to elect) currently rests on a single scored execution with its control.
